A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldMem and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures and supplementary materials. Content can be matched across the substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Minecraft and RealEstate10K experiments, qualitative simulations and ablations, including supplementary memory-length and pose-prediction results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, plus new measurements of retrieval latency and training/inference resource usage.

M1.justification: The DiT/Diffusion Forcing backbone, frame/state memory bank, FOV/time-based retrieval, similarity filtering, state-conditioned attention and pose predictor remain. The token-level and state-aware descriptions clarify the existing mechanism; sinusoidal timestamp encoding was already shown in v1 Figure 10.

E1.justification: Both versions use Minecraft/MineDojo for navigation and interaction and RealEstate10K for scene-revisitation consistency. The revised trajectory protocol and training-set size do not establish a distinct new task, population or environment.

E2.justification: The RealEstate10K comparison expands from DFoT alone in v1 Table 2 to DFoT, CameraCtrl, TrajAttn and Viewcrafter in v2 Table 4. This substantially broadens comparison to camera-controlled generation and explicit reconstruction methods. Minecraft comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported Minecraft training changes from 20K to 12K videos, 640×320 to 640×360 resolution, and 200K steps on eight GPUs to 500K on four GPUs; batch size per GPU changes from two to four. The retrieval weight changes from 0.2tc to 0.2/tc. RealEstate evaluation changes from 100 full-rotation samples to five return trajectories of 37–60 frames across 100 scenes. New resource comparisons specify an H200 and 20 denoising steps. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Section 7.2 adds a substantive investigation of scalability: retrieval latency across 10–1000 memory candidates and training/inference cost with versus without memory. The timestamp ablation is now described as covering both retrieval and embedding. The sampling-strategy, memory-length and pose-prediction studies already existed in v1; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The newly reported average retrieval times do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Most Minecraft PSNR values decrease by exactly 6 dB, including WorldMem beyond-context PSNR from 25.32 to 19.32, while its LPIPS/rFID remain 0.1429/15.37; beyond-context DF remains 18.04 PSNR. Ablation tables and the long-term PSNR plot are also revised. RealEstate results are replaced under the revised protocol: WorldMem PSNR changes from 20.19 to 23.34 and DFoT from 8.396 to 16.42, alongside new comparator results. New profiling reports retrieval times of 0.04–0.16 seconds. These changes do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The diffusion, attention, masking, camera-pose and Monte Carlo overlap mathematics remain substantively equivalent. Noise-level equations become prose, and supplementary symbols are renamed. Explicit sinusoidal timestamp notation restates the encoding already documented in v1; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The main claims about long-term scene consistency, reconstruction across viewpoint/time gaps and dynamic-world simulation persist. The revised introduction adds an explicit claimed advantage that standard attention allows the memory mechanism to scale with hardware and model capacity, modestly extending the contribution's stated scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly qualifies RealEstate10K as short, non-interactive and temporally limited, and attributes Viewcrafter's limitations to reconstruction/rendering errors. It also interprets measured memory overhead and asserts deployment potential through acceleration. The original limitations concerning occlusion, interaction realism and linear memory growth are retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: v2 adds memory-bank tensor shape and float32 storage information, H200 hardware and timing settings, and revised training/hyperparameter disclosures. Conversely, it removes v1's 4,800-frame rFID sample count and RealEstate details specifying memory-only fine-tuning with two context frames and one memory frame. These materially alter reproducibility information; the project-page address remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around geometry-free memory, fixed-token scene representations and exact scene recall versus temporal smoothness or semantic coherence. New discussions cite SRT, Rayzer, GenFusion, MEMO, CORGI and Make-a-Story, among others. DUSt3R, IP-Adapter and ControlNet citations disappear. These changes exceed citation-style or bibliography updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanation are substantially rewritten, with v1 Sections 3.3–3.5 reorganized into representation/retrieval and state-aware conditioning sections. Experimental details, the sampling ablation and limitations move from the supplement into the main text. Terminology and captions are revised, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column format with extensive float rearrangement. Figure 2 replaces the temporal-block panel with a state-embedding panel; the RealEstate comparison is replaced and expanded; the FOV visualization moves to the supplement; and resource tables are added. The long-term PSNR plot's axis changes from 15–30 to 9–24.

improvement.justification: The broader RealEstate comparison, including a reconstruction baseline, and explicit memory/latency measurements make v2 more informative about comparative effectiveness and practical cost. These provide a limited net improvement. Benefits are tempered by unexplained systematic PSNR revisions, lost RealEstate reproduction details and an approximately 10 FPS acceleration claim without documented validation; higher reported scores do not establish a performance advance.
